facts.statement: Lariosaurus was first discovered at Perledo on Lake Como in 1830 and named in 1847 by Curioni.
facts.quote: First discovered at Perledo on the Lake Como in 1830, it was named in 1847 by Curioni

facts.statement: A complete specimen of L. xingyiensis measured 70.5 cm long, while L. hongguoensis may have reached up to 80 cm, making it one of the smallest known nothosaurs.
facts.quote: With a complete specimen of L. xingyiensis measuring 70.5 cm long and L. hongguoensis possibly measuring up to 80 cm long, it was one of the smallest known nothosaurs.

facts.statement: The name Lariosaurus means "Lizard from Larius", referring to the ancient name of Lake Como.
facts.quote: its name meaning "Lizard from Larius", the ancient name of the lake.

facts.statement: Lariosaurus was a primitive nothosaur characterized by a short neck and small flippers compared to its relatives.
facts.quote: For a nothosaur, Lariosaurus was primitive, possessing a short neck and small flippers in comparison to its relatives.

facts.statement: Due to its short neck and small flippers, Lariosaurus was likely a poor swimmer that spent much time on land or hunting in shallow waters.
facts.quote: This would have made it a relatively poor swimmer, and it is presumed to have spent much time on dry land, or hunting in shallows.

facts.statement: Lariosaurus had strongly elongated premaxillary and anterior dentary teeth resembling fangs that likely functioned as a fish trap.
facts.quote: The premaxillary and anterior dentary teeth are strongly elongated, like fangs, and could have acted as a 'fish trap'.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Lariosaurus were pachyostotic and possessed low neural spines.
facts.quote: The vertebrae are pachyostotic and have a low neural spine.

facts.statement: Lariosaurus had gastral ribs composed of multiple elements that formed a sturdy type of armor.
facts.quote: The gastral ribs are made up of multiple elements and form a sturdy kind of armour.

facts.statement: A Lariosaurus skeleton containing two juvenile Cyamodus placodonts in its stomach provides evidence of its diet.
facts.quote: Another Lariosaurus skeleton was found with two juvenile placodonts of the genus Cyamodus in its stomach, giving an indication of its diet.

facts.statement: Based on findings of immature skeletons inside adults, many believe Lariosaurus was viviparous and capable of bearing live young.
facts.quote: based on skeletal findings of immature lariosaurs inside the adults, Lariosaurus is believed by many to be viviparous, or able to bear live young.

facts.statement: Lariosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic (late Anisian to late Ladinian stages) in central and western Europe and China.
facts.quote: Lariosaurus is an extinct genus of nothosaurid from the Middle Triassic (late Anisian to late Ladinian stage) of central and western Europe and China.

facts.statement: While Rieppel synonymized Lariosaurus, Silvestrosaurus, and Ceresiosaurus in 1998, many authors dispute this and consider them close relatives instead.
facts.quote: In 1998 Rieppel synonymised Lariosaurus, Silvestrosaurus and Ceresiosaurus, but this is disputed by many authors and they are usually considered close relatives.

facts.statement: Some sources indicate that the size of Lariosaurus did not exceed 60 cm in length.
facts.quote: Su tamaño no superaba los 60 cm de longitud.

facts.statement: Lariosaurus likely spent much of its life swimming in shallow waters or on the shore, catching small prey like fish, shrimp, crabs, and worms, or scavenging reptile eggs.
facts.quote: Al parecer, pasaba gran parte de su vida nadando en aguas poco profundas o fuera, en la orilla, atrapando pequeñas presas como peces, gambas, camarones, y gusanos de las charcas costeras o rapiñando huevos de reptiles (en su época no existían las aves).
